MS MAPLESURE INSURANCE Group Benefits Digital Experience BUSINESS REQUIREMENT DOCUMENT · ENHANCEMENT Request ID REQ-2026-134 Raised by Group Benefits Digital Experience, MapleSure Insurance Business owner D. Okafor Domain Plan Sponsor Digital Access Target application SponsorConnect (plan sponsor portal) Type Enhancement — replaces the shared-credential entry to an existing application Priority High Requested date 2026-09-07

## Business objective

Give every plan sponsor user a personal, secure login page for SponsorConnect — so that each sponsor administrator signs in as themselves, MapleSure can attribute every claim submission to a named person, and the online disability claim submission journey can go live on a trusted front door. Plan sponsors are the employer organisations that sponsor coverage for their members. Today a sponsor's HR team shares one organisation-level password to reach SponsorConnect, which means MapleSure cannot say who uploaded a claim form, who viewed a member's status, or when a departed employee's access was actually removed.

## Background and current state

SponsorConnect is an existing application. It currently authenticates with a single credential per sponsor organisation, issued by the onboarding team and passed around the sponsor's HR staff by email. Individual user records already exist in the sponsor administration back office (name, work email, sponsor organisation, role), but nothing in the portal uses them to sign a person in. The online disability claim submission programme (EPIC-S7-001) needs a named submitter on every claim. Its compliance review will not approve go-live while the portal cannot identify the individual who submitted a claim on a member's behalf. Support volume for "we lost the sponsor password" is the second most common sponsor contact, and every reset re-issues one shared credential to the whole organisation.

## Requirements


1. Personal login page. A sponsor user signs in on a single, clearly branded MapleSure login page with their work email address and a personal password; the shared organisation credential is retired at cut-over and no longer accepted.

2. Sponsor context on sign-in. A successful sign-in establishes the user's sponsor organisation and portal role (Sponsor Administrator or HR User) from the sponsor administration record, and the portal header shows the signed-in person's name and their organisation's plan number.

3. Multi-sponsor users. A user who is authorised for more than one sponsor organisation (a benefits consultant, for example) is shown a choice of organisation immediately after sign-in and acts within only the one chosen for that session.

4. Generic failure message. A failed sign-in shows one generic message — it must not reveal whether the email address is known, or whether the password was wrong.

5. Temporary lockout. After five consecutive failed attempts for the same email address, sign-in for that address is locked for fifteen minutes; the page says so without confirming the address exists, and a Sponsor Administrator can see the lockout in their user list.

6. Self-serve password reset. A "Forgotten your password?" link sends a single-use reset link to the user's registered work email address, valid for thirty minutes; the page's response is the same whether or not the address is registered.

7. Session timeout. A signed-in session expires after twenty minutes of inactivity, with a warning shown two minutes before, and the user is returned to the login page with an explanation rather than an error.

8. Access removal. When a Sponsor Administrator deactivates a user in the sponsor administration record, that user cannot sign in from that moment, and any active session for them ends within five minutes.

9. Audit log. Every sign-in attempt, lockout, password reset request and session expiry is recorded with the email address, sponsor organisation, timestamp, outcome and originating network address — and never the password or the reset link.

10. Accessibility. The login and organisation-choice pages are fully keyboard-accessible, label every field, announce errors to assistive technology, and meet WCAG AA contrast on the MapleSure palette.

11. Credential storage. Passwords are never stored or logged in plain text; the credential store holds salted hashes only, and reset links are stored only as a hash of the token.

## Out of scope

Multi-factor authentication and federation with sponsor employers' own identity providers (planned as a following phase once individual accounts exist). Sponsor user creation, role assignment and deactivation screens — these already exist in the sponsor administration back office; this request only makes the portal honour them. Member-facing sign-in, which is delivered separately under REQ-2026-121. Any change to the claim submission forms themselves.

## Success measures

Every claim submitted through SponsorConnect after cut-over carries the named sponsor user who submitted it. The shared organisation credential is refused on every sponsor account from the cut-over date. A user with valid personal credentials reaches their sponsor's portal home in one attempt; a multi-sponsor user reaches the organisation choice in one attempt. Invalid attempts and reset requests never disclose whether an email address is registered. "Lost sponsor password" contacts fall by at least half within one quarter of cut-over. Zero passwords or reset tokens in any log or audit record.

## Notes for delivery

This is an enhancement to a live application, not a new one: reuse the existing sponsor administration user records as the source of truth for identity and role, and keep the change to the login page, the organisation-choice step, the session handling and the audit log. The existing shared-credential path stays behind a feature switch until cut-over so the two can run side by side during sponsor migration. Synthetic sponsor and user data only.

## Sign-off
